binders: A measurable sample space Ω and a probability measure μ on it.
A natural-number-indexed family X of real-valued random variables.
Real parameters m and σ, with σ strictly positive.
A natural sample-size parameter N tending to infinity and an arbitrary real threshold t.
hypotheses: Every Xᵢ is square-integrable under μ.
The family X is mutually independent.
Every Xᵢ has the same distribution as X₀.
The integral of X₀ is m.
The variance of X₀ is σ².
conclusions: For every real t, the probability that the normalized centered sum of X₀ through X_N is at most t converges, as N tends to infinity, to the standard-normal cumulative probability at t.
mathematical_definitions: The normalized sum at index N is (σ√(N+1))⁻¹ times the sum of Xᵢ−m over i=0,…,N.
Each probability law is the pushforward of μ under the normalized sum.
The limiting law is the Gaussian probability measure with mean zero and variance one.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let Ω be a measurable space, let μ be a probability measure on Ω, and let X₀, X₁, … be real-valued random variables. Fix real numbers m and σ with σ > 0. Assume every Xᵢ belongs to L²(μ), the family is independent, every Xᵢ has the same distribution as X₀, the integral of X₀ is m, and the variance of X₀ is σ². Then, for every real t, as N tends to infinity, the probability that (1/(σ√(N+1))) times the sum of Xᵢ−m over i = 0,…,N is at most t converges to the probability that a standard normal random variable is at most t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index set is all natural numbers, and each partial sum contains the first N+1 variables.
The underlying measure is required to be a probability measure.
Each variable must be in L²(μ), incorporating measurability and a finite second moment.
The scaling parameter σ is strictly positive and the variance is exactly σ².
Convergence is asserted for every real threshold using closed lower half-lines.
The universally quantified theorem is vacuous for choices of data whose hypotheses cannot all be inhabited.
No inconsistency is apparent among the assumptions.
No convergence rate or quantitative error bound is asserted.
No moment beyond the second is assumed.
No almost-sure, L², or pointwise convergence of the normalized sums is asserted.
The proposition states pointwise CDF convergence rather than explicitly naming weak convergence.
